messages:
rachael: heads up — i'm running an off-hours dry-run of the DB backup rotation and key escrow flow, want to confirm RBAC/audit expectations before i proceed.
kevin: thanks — what's the failure mode we're validating? key unavailability, restore path, or audit provenance?
rachael: mostly key unavailability + verifying we can still list+restore snapshots when CMKs are rotated. also want to ensure audit logs clearly show who requested the restore and which key was used.
alex: for the rotation scenario, we need both the KMS grant and a temporary role that can assume access to the re-encrypted snapshots. otherwise restores will 403. short: RBAC + KMS policy must align.
anya: can you paste the current IAM snippet you're using? small differences in sts:AssumeRole vs kms:Decrypt matter.
rachael: sure — current snippet i'm testing with (redacted):
```
{
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt", "kms:GenerateDataKey"],
  "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01"
}
```
kevin: ok. two quick notes: 1) ensure the snapshot export role also has s3:PutObject for the backup bucket; 2) add kms:DescribeKey to help diagnostics in logs.
security-oncall: also add iam:PassRole for the export service principal — otherwise the job will fail earlier and auth logs will be confusing.
rachael: good catch. any thoughts on key escrow / emergency access? current proposal is HSM-backed CMKs + an escrow key in a different account with strict approver workflow (2 ppl + pager duty) — looking for feedback.
mike: escrow in separate account is good for blast radius. make sure cross-account KMS grants are explicit and recorded in our audit stream. prefer a short-lived grant with kms:CreateGrant + kms:RetireGrant in the workflow.
anya: +1. Also, add a CloudTrail data event filter so we capture S3 GetObject on encrypted backups — sometimes teams miss those and then wonder why restore failed.
kevin: about audit provenance — include both CloudTrail management events and S3 data events. tag the restore job with request_id and include that in the KMS encryption_context; that'll link the KMS and S3 events.
rachael: example encryption_context i'm planning:
```
{"restore_request_id": "${REQUEST_ID}", "initiator": "rachael@redwood.com", "env": "prod"}
```
security-oncall: perfect. that makes post-incident correlation way easier.
infra-bot: scheduled job started: db-backup-rotate-dryrun at 2025-11-05T02:00:34Z (job id: jb-87123)
rachael: running step 1: simulate CMK rotate (create new key alias, attach policy, re-encrypt snapshot metadata). will follow up with logs.
kevin: when you hit the re-encrypt step, watch for kms:NotFound vs AccessDenied in logs — those lead to different playbook paths.
rachael: saw kms:AccessDenied on first attempt. i added kms:DescribeKey + kms:CreateGrant for export role and re-ran — now re-encrypt moved forward.
anya: did CloudTrail show the CreateGrant event? we should capture grant_id in the run output.
rachael: yes — cloudtrail entry shows CreateGrant with grantId g-0a1b2c3d. added to run log.
mike: next step: test restore from another account with the escrow key. i'll try to assume the escrow role and pull the snapshot.
infra-bot: cross-account assume-role attempt from acct-4444 by mike succeeded (sts:AssumeRole) at 2025-11-05T02:04:10Z
mike: restore succeeded using escrow key, but S3 putObject latencies spiked — probably chunked upload + sidecar encryption. worth adding a note to runbook about throttle risk during restores.
security-oncall: capture that in the incident runbook notes: "restore load may impact production read replicas" and include an explicit traffic-shift step.
rachael: overall dry-run status: re-encrypt ✅, cross-account escrow restore ✅, audit entries linked ✅, minor perf note on S3 puts. i'll open a small PR to update the playbook with IAM snippet, grant steps, cloudtrail filters, and the throttle note.
kevin: ping me on the PR for a quick review — looks good.
rachael: thanks everyone. closing out, will post PR link when ready. :thumbsup:
